candidates.name: Madelung's disease
support_spans: progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the right side of her nose and right cheek
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement are consistent with Madelung's disease, a rare condition characterized by the growth of fatty tissue in the neck and shoulder region.

candidates.name: Nerve sheath tumor
support_spans: subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density
candidates.why: The presence of spindle cells with bland cytomorphology and ill-defined cytoplasm is consistent with a nerve sheath tumor, which can cause facial asymmetry and skin thickening.

candidates.name: Lipomatosis
support_spans: mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue
candidates.why: The extension of mature adipocytes into skeletal tissue suggests a diagnosis of lipomatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of fatty tissue in abnormal locations.

candidates.name: Fibrolipomatosis
candidates.why: The presence of thickened and fragmented collagen bundles is consistent with fibrolipomatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of fibrous and fatty tissue.
